bull_bear.body: Debt reduction priority (leverage to normalize by Q2FY27). Final dividend INR 2/share. No major M&A; focus on 'asset sweating' post-capex cycle. Internal accruals funded ~75% of recent capex surge.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Coking coal price volatility (Q1 headwind guided). Delay in slurry pipeline or DRI-2 commissioning. Global steel oversupply (China exports). Execution risk in shifting mix to 70% flats without approval delays. Further impairments ruled out for Australia.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume ramp-up and market demand (9%+ India growth); Pragmatic on margin compression due to mix/costs; Decisive on writing off Australian assets to clean up balance sheet; Focused on operational efficiency ('asset sweating').
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The impairment of the Australian asset is final with no further cash outflow expected, yet the license is retained. The shift to 70% flat products is a deliberate strategic pivot to become a 'one-stop shop' for infrastructure clients, accepting lower per-tonne margins for higher absolute volume and stickiness. The slurry pipeline savings are per-tonne of steel produced, not just iron ore transported, amplifying the EBITDA impact.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Framework commits to funding primarily via internal accruals, maintaining INR 2,000 cr liquidity and keeping net debt to EBITDA below 1.5x through the cycle; current status is cash of INR 6,080 cr and net debt/EBITDA of 1.71x - above its own through-cycle ceiling.
- Dividend commitment is "To reward shareholders after meeting growth capital requirements"; the company "Declared 200% dividend in FY26 while investing in growth capex".
- Deleveraging track record: net debt/EBITDA fell from 4.56x (FY20) to 0.57x (FY22) before rising to 1.66x (FY26) and 1.71x (Q1FY27); net debt moved from INR 35,918 cr (FY20) to INR 15,927 cr (Q1FY27).
- Debt/equity has stayed low - 1.2x (FY20) to 0.41x (Q1FY27); the Q1FY27 net-debt bridge shows INR 1,125 cr long-term debt raised against INR 1,119 cr repayment and INR 268 cr of short-term loans, with capital acceptances of INR 369 cr at Jun'26 and INR 300 cr at Mar'26 excluded from the bridge.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated value chain from captive raw materials (iron ore mines at Kasia, Tensa and Roida-I; non-coking and coking coal capacities) through iron making, steelmaking, rolling and downstream processing
- India's largest technologically advanced Hot Strip Mill with 6 MTPA annual production capacity
- Strategically located five-site manufacturing footprint (Raigarh, Raipur, Angul, Barbil, Patratu) supporting logistics and cost competitiveness
- Diversified, value-added product portfolio spanning long and flat/plate products serving strategic sectors including defence, railways and infrastructure
- Established retail distribution network under the JINDAL PANTHER brand alongside a predominantly B2B/institutional customer base
- Post year-end credit rating upgrade (CARE AA to AA+, Stable) reflecting strengthening balance sheet and credit profile
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Impaired/stranded overseas coking coal asset in Australia — The Australian mine remained non-operational and under care and maintenance during FY 2025-26; a comprehensive reassessment found the mining shaft has been sealed, and the Company recognised a non-cash impairment charge reflecting the reassessment of the asset's recoverable value in line with current operational realities.
- Loss-making South Africa operations amid a high-cost environment — South Africa operations faced subdued market conditions, operational constraints and a high cost environment during FY 2025-26; anthracite coal production fell sharply year-on-year and both EBITDA and PAT remained negative and widened versus the prior year, with the Company still evaluating operational improvements and cost optimisation to sustain the asset long-term.
- Commodity and energy price volatility driven by geopolitical shocks — Brent crude swung sharply in early CY2026 (to around US$120/bbl in April 2026 from US$69/bbl average in CY2025) following Middle East conflict and disruption risk to the Strait of Hormuz, illustrating the Company's exposure to volatile input/energy costs and shipping-route disruption beyond its control.
- Dependence on trade-protection measures against Chinese steel overcapacity — Domestic price realisations and import competition remain tied to the continuation of the 12% safeguard duty on select steel imports (in force till April 2028); persistent global overcapacity, particularly from China, and evolving tariff/non-tariff barriers globally keep international trade flows and Indian steel pricing exposed to policy shifts.
- Rising finance costs pressuring standalone interest coverage — The standalone Interest Coverage Ratio declined versus the prior year due to a decrease in EBITDA and an increase in net finance charges during the year ended 31 March 2026, alongside a decline in standalone Operating Margin and Net Profit Margin, indicating margin and debt-servicing headroom is narrowing even as the balance sheet funds a large expansion programme.
- Cyber security — The Risk Management Committee's charter specifically calls out cyber security as a particular area of risk assessment, monitoring and review, reflecting the Company's exposure to cyber threats across its integrated, multi-site manufacturing and IT/OT operations.
- Operational complexity of global operations across multiple geographies — The Company operates raw-material and coal assets across India, Mozambique, South Africa and Australia; performance has diverged sharply by geography (e.g., Mozambique improved while South Africa and Australia weakened/impaired), exposing consolidated results to country-specific operational, cost and regulatory conditions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Four self-described pillars: Growth Focussed (scaling world-class integrated capacity), Strong Financials ("Best in class balance sheet", "Most diversified product portfolio", "Industry leading EBITDA per tonne"), Sustainability Driven, and Industry 4.0 & AI.
- Renamed from Jindal Steel & Power Limited to Jindal Steel Limited; CARE upgraded the long-term credit rating from AA/stable to AA+/stable during Q1FY27.
- Assets are described as built "across an integrated value chain" spanning captive iron ore and coal, iron making, liquid steel and both flat and long finished-steel mills.
- Industry framing places India as the strongest growth market - Indian steel demand of 160 MT in CY25 rising to 172 MT (CY26E) and 187 MT (CY27E) against a Chinese decline from 796 MT to 784 MT (World Steel Association Short Range Outlook, Apr 2026).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Digital & AI] Enterprise AI rollout is unified by JARVIS (Jindal AI for Real time Visibility, Intelligence & Systems), "one governed, Jindal-owned platform" across three layers - Personal AI (AIKSHAM assistant), Functional AI (department agents in sales, HR, procurement, finance, planning) and Industrial AI (digital twins, predictive models, video analytics, experimenting with humanoids).
- [Digital roadmap] Named initiatives include AI prediction models for the blast furnace, digital twin expansion to SMS, an Integrated Terminal Operating System for the port (kicked off), a unified procurement system (kicked off), CRM plant automation with SAP, and a customer self-service portal for order visibility.
- [India market backdrop] India was a net importer in Q1FY27 with net imports of 0.5 MT, "marking the second consecutive quarter of net import position"; finished steel imports rose 49% YoY to 2.1 MT while exports were 1.6 MT.
- [Price environment] Domestic Mumbai HRC averaged INR 58,627/t in Q1FY27 (up INR 6,896 YoY, INR 4,869 QoQ) while TMT was INR 57,115/t (down INR 92 QoQ), with the deck noting "TMT shifted to a discount to HRC towards the end of the quarter due to seasonal weakness"; premium HCC Australia was USD 261/t.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Jindal Steel is an integrated steel producer with backward integration into captive iron ore mining and forward integration into rolling and downstream processing, manufacturing a wide range of long steel products and specialised plate solutions. Its products serve defence and shipbuilding, railways, construction and infrastructure, energy (wind, hydro, thermal), oil and gas, general engineering and OEM customers, alongside a retail rebar brand for individual home builders. The company sells predominantly in the domestic market across 28 states and also exports to more than 35 countries.

- **Long Steel Products:** Wire rods, Bar rods, Rail & Universal beams, Special profiles
- **Flat/Plate Products:** Hot rolled coils, Plates, CRM (cold rolled) products
- **Retail:** JINDAL PANTHER rebars

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scaling for the next phase of growth by leveraging the larger, integrated manufacturing platform at Angul (emerging as one of the world's largest single-location steel plants) to increase volumes, expand value-added offerings and enhance operating efficiencies
- Strengthening raw material security through strategic investments in iron ore and coal assets to enhance self-sufficiency, reduce exposure to market volatility and improve cost competitiveness
- Driving growth through value-added products by increasing focus on specialised and value-added products and investing in flat products and downstream facilities to expand into automotive, engineering, infrastructure and construction segments
- Building structural cost advantages via infrastructure investments (slurry pipeline, dedicated port infrastructure, surplus captive power capacity) to reduce logistics costs and support margin sustainability
- Maintaining strong cash generation and financial discipline to fund one of the largest expansion programmes in the Company's history while preserving a resilient balance sheet
- Embedding sustainability into the growth journey, with a Net Zero ambition by 2047, a target to cut CO2 emissions intensity, coal gasification and slurry pipeline projects for resource efficiency, and a 'Zero Harm' safety philosophy backed by strengthened ESG governance
- The Company manages financial capital through disciplined capital allocation, prudent risk management and a focus on operational performance, seeking to balance growth, profitability and financial resilience as market conditions evolve. Cash generation, liquidity and balance-sheet capacity are directed to support investment in capacity expansion, asset modernisation and other projects intended to strengthen long-term competitiveness, and also to support sustainability and decarbonisation priorities such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, resource productivity and low-carbon technologies. On dividends, the Board has framed a Dividend Distribution Policy under SEBI Listing Regulations that establishes the parameters considered before declaring or recommending a dividend, and has recommended a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share (face value Rs 1) for FY 2025-26; no amount was transferred to reserves during the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 marked the successful completion of Phase II of the Angul Integrated Steel Plant, taking installed crude steelmaking capacity to 15.6 MTPA (12.0 MTPA at Angul and 3.6 MTPA at Raigarh). During the year the Company commissioned the 4.6 MTPA Blast Furnace 'Bhagavati Subhadrika', 3.0 MTPA BOF-2 and 3.0 MTPA BOF-3, operationalised both modules of the Shree Bhoomi Power Plant (2 x 525 MW), commissioned a 1.2 MTPA Cold Rolling Mill complex, and completed the pipe conveyor system connecting the Utkal mines with the Angul steel plant. The 192-km Barbil-Angul slurry pipeline is nearing completion, expected to reduce transportation dependency, logistics costs and emissions once operational. Development of the Paradip Port berth is continuing, with commissioning and ramp-up planned in a phased manner from FY 2026-27 onwards. As of March 31, 2026, the Company had incurred cumulative capital expenditure of Rs 35,498 crore out of a total planned investment of Rs 47,043 crore for its integrated expansion programme, with the remaining capex expected to support completion, integration and ramp-up of ongoing projects. On raw materials, the Company progressed the Thakurani-A1 and Roida-I iron ore blocks and the Saradhapur Jalatap East and Utkal B1 coal blocks to strengthen captive resource security alongside its existing Kasia, Tensa, Gare Palma IV/6 and Utkal C assets. Separately, in the overseas coal portfolio, the Company reassessed its Australian mine (previously under care and maintenance) and, given the mining shaft has been sealed, recognised a non-cash impairment reflecting a prudent reassessment of recoverable value; its Mozambique and South Africa operations remained stable with no material change in structure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's infrastructure, manufacturing and energy transition ambitions are expected to support sustained steel demand growth
- Government capital expenditure of Rs 11.21 lakh crore across roads, railways, metro systems, airports, ports, urban infrastructure and renewable energy/industrial corridors is creating sustained demand for structural steel, rails, plates and specialised products
- As the scale and complexity of infrastructure projects increases, demand increasingly favours steelmakers capable of delivering specialised products, integrated supply chains and consistent execution at scale
- Domestic iron ore prices are expected to remain well supported over the medium term as domestic iron ore production is not expected to increase commensurately with steel production growth
- India's expanding steelmaking capacity is expected to sustain demand for imported premium coking coal over the medium term, despite efforts to diversify sourcing and strengthen raw material security, given limited domestic high-quality metallurgical coal
- Indian HRC and TMT prices declined in the first three quarters of FY 2025-26 on lower-priced imports but recovered in the final quarter, supported by improving domestic demand and the 12% safeguard duty on select flat steel imports effective 21 April 2025
- Global steel prices are expected to be influenced by developments in China's steel sector, infrastructure investment, trade policy measures and raw material/energy price movements, with geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global overcapacity keeping regional pricing dynamic
- Supplied high-strength, high-performance customised plates for the Atal Setu (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link), India's longest sea bridge
- Supplied high-strength, high-performance customised plates for the Versova-Bandra Sea Link urban mobility project
- Contributed steel to the Agra Metro Rail public transport project
- Contributed to large-scale urban infrastructure development under the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA)
- Contributed to the Nagpur Metro Rail Corporation project
- Supplied high-strength quenched and tempered (Q&T) steel plates for penstock applications on the Ratle Hydroelectric Power Project
- Supplied high-strength quenched and tempered (Q&T) steel plates for penstock applications on the Dibang Hydroelectric Power Project
- Supplied high-impact, high-strength boiler quality steel plates for the Reliance Refinery Expansion Project
- Supplied high-impact, high-strength boiler quality steel plates for the Bina Refinery Expansion Project
- Contributed product to the Prayagraj Railway Station Redevelopment project
- Ongoing supply relationship supporting Konkan Railway infrastructure

deepdive.thesis: Jindal Steel completed a transformative capacity expansion to 15.6 MTPA in FY26, driving volume growth but compressing per-tonne EBITDA due to startup costs and coking coal inflation. The key inflection point is FY27, where the commissioning of the slurry pipeline (INR 750-1,000/tonne savings) and stabilization of the new Angul assets are expected to restore margins despite a strategic shift toward lower-margin flat products.

open.item: Utkal B2 coal to be with the company at the start of Q3FY26 (some monsoon delays).
Full potential of the expanded Angul capacity to be realized towards end of FY26 and partly early FY27.
Paradip Port berth development to continue, with commissioning and ramp-up planned in a phased manner from FY 2026-27 onwards
Coking coal prices expected to increase by $20 to $25 per tonne sequentially in Q1FY27.
Rail-rake program of ~79 rakes; 72 acquired, remaining to be delivered within next 2-3 months.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil to Angul) close to completion, expected to be commissioned in Q1FY27; ~INR 700/tonne of iron ore savings (~INR 750-1,000/tonne of steel as ramped).
Net debt (INR 16,019 cr, net debt/EBITDA 1.66x) leverage metrics expected to normalize by Q2FY27 as new capacities ramp.
1,050 MW SBPP ramp-up to complete within H1FY27; excess power to be sold in merchant market (not material) while providing captive stability and redundancy.
Pellet Plant-2 remains a key project to be commissioned, targeted for FY27.
Value-added share (fell to ~61% from 66% QoQ during ramp-up) to return to normal robust levels and improve as capacity utilization is achieved and downstream/heat-treated plate capacities grow.
DRI-2 (2 million tonnes, under construction) expected towards the end of FY27.
FY27 sales guidance of 10.5 million to 11 million tonnes.
FY27 production plan of 11 million to 11.5 million tonnes.
BOF3 expected to run at ~60%-66% capacity utilization in FY27 even before DRI-2 metallics come online.
DRI-2 (associated metallic capacity for BOF3) targeted for FY27-end, unchanged.
DRI-2 timeline revised into FY27.
Pellet Plant-2 (6mt) expected to come up in FY27.
FY27 reiterated as a full year of full ramp-up of the expanded capacity.
Full ramp-up of the expanded capacity targeted for FY27.
Capex program largely complete; FY27/FY28 to allocate INR 7,500-10,000 crores/year for sustenance capex, shifting focus to asset sweating.
